key_insight: The paper shows that the linear Poisson source for wall-pressure fluctuations stays O(1) in inner scaling at very high Reynolds number, so it cannot explain the observed logarithmic growth of wall-pressure variance.
engineering_relevance: This narrows the origin of high-Reynolds-number wall-pressure amplification to the nonlinear source, improving turbulence-model and near-wall noise-prediction physics.
method: Used simultaneous velocity and velocity-gradient hot-wire data from Zimmermann et al. (2019).
Compared a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer with a high-Reynolds-number pipe flow.
Examined the inner-scaled factors in the linear pressure-source term across Reynolds number.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports collapse of the inner-scaled linear-source factors across Reynolds number and an inertial-layer gradient variance that decays approximately as the inverse of wall distance.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on indirect source-term analysis and assumes the measured gradients and inner scaling remain representative as $\delta^+$ approaches asymptotically large values.
paper_title: An Inner-Scaled Linear Contribution to Wall-Pressure Variance at High Reynolds Number
